content.content:
Apply this criterion to the repository-root README.md and the decision node nsyxzxzr that commits to it, reading them against the seven prerequisites uuutyrzs, rzkvnnll, oxxwkrvo, ynmpvmmp, rolozxtn, vqultolm and vutylkzu. Fail with a finding that names the offending part and, where a prerequisite bears on it, the prerequisite it fails against.

1. COMPLETENESS FLOOR AND COMPOSITION BOUND.
- Completeness floor: README.md exists at the repository root and has a title, an opening introduction, and all four named sections — Getting started, Features, Development and License — each present and non-empty. A missing or empty README.md, a placeholder decision node, or a missing or empty required part leaves that part of the composition with no subject and is a finding naming the missing part.
- Composition bound: those four sections are the whole of the document below the introduction. Any additional section, heading or appendix of any kind (such as Troubleshooting, Installation, Requirements, Contributing or Roadmap) is a finding naming that part. The document carries no installation, build, packaging, marketplace or troubleshooting guidance anywhere; any such instruction is a finding naming the claim.

2. SECTION SUBJECT FLOORS AND LICENCES AGAINST THE PREREQUISITES.
Every claim in README.md and in nsyxzxzr's rationale must be licensed by the corresponding prerequisite, and each part of README.md must carry the subject its prerequisite commits to rather than merely avoiding contradiction:
- Title and introduction (uuutyrzs): the README's title and its opening introduction name the extension by the identity uuutyrzs records — `deccy-viewer`, displayed to readers as "Deccy Viewer" — and by no other identity. The title displays the name as uuutyrzs records it being displayed, "Deccy Viewer"; the introduction identifies the extension it describes by the recorded package name `deccy-viewer` or the recorded display name "Deccy Viewer" and states uuutyrzs's subject — that it is a Visual Studio Code (VS Code) extension that visualises the deccy graph of a project — adding no claim beyond that subject (no installation, configuration, settings, requirements, supported platforms or versions, or marketplace claims). A title or introduction that carries an identity the extension no longer has, or any name uuutyrzs does not record, contradicts uuutyrzs and is a finding naming the offending name and the part it appears in. The statement uuutyrzs's rationale records — that the extension helps visualise the connections of nodes beyond what a jj graph can show — lies within that subject: an introduction may state it, and its absence is not a finding.
- Getting started (rzkvnnll): the Getting started section tells the reader to open the graph with the 'Deccy: Open Deccy Graph' command from the Command Palette or from that command's editor title bar entry, which is shown while the graph webview panel is the active webview panel, and adds no other command, keybinding, surface or setup step.
- Features (oxxwkrvo): the Features section covers all five user-visible feature areas that oxxwkrvo commits to: (a) the interactive graph in a panel, drawn with boxes for decisions, rounded boxes for evaluations, solid dependency edges and dashed evaluation edges each with a single arrowhead at the child end, unresolved edges visibly marked, and each node's box displaying only its label from the jj change description; (b) text search: pressing '/' with no modifier opens a focused search field without changing the current selection, pan or zoom, typing a query marks every node whose id, label or content contains the query case-insensitively and marks none when the query is empty, pressing Enter and Shift+Enter steps to the next and previous marked node in graph order wrapping at either end, and pressing Esc closes the field and clears the search marks and selection; (c) the detail panel's three labelled sections — Kind, Content and Rationale — shown in that fixed order for every selection (with empty sections still shown with their labels when mentioned); (d) the Content section's type-based formatting while keeping the section's label and place and leaving Kind and Rationale unchanged: narrative prose shown as wrapped running text with paragraph breaks preserved and no code framing, structured or code content and any other content types shown verbatim in a monospaced block labelled with the content type with line breaks and indentation preserved and without refusing or hiding unrecognised types, and file-referenced content showing the content type and referenced file paths in that block; and (e) the four labelled relationship sections — 'depends_on', 'evaluates', 'dependents' and 'evaluators' — listing related node ids for the selected node's prerequisites, evaluated nodes (empty for a decision), dependents and evaluators, with empty sections showing an explicit empty state. Omitting or garbling any of these five areas is a finding naming the missing fact and oxxwkrvo. Adding any unrecorded feature claim — such as an alternative way of opening or dismissing search, another match rule or traversal order, a visible node id or secondary label on a box, section or node collapse/expand behaviour, placement of the search field or relationship sections on the page or relative to Kind, Content and Rationale, match highlight styling, reload or persistence behaviour, per-type syntax highlighting or extra fields beyond the recorded renderings, how a listed relationship id's node content is rendered, or a fifth relationship section or reversed direction — is a finding naming the claim and oxxwkrvo.
- Development (ynmpvmmp): the Development section explains that a fresh clone runs with a single VS Code debug session, with no manual build, install or packaging.
- License (rolozxtn): the License section states that the extension is licensed under Apache-2.0 and points readers at the LICENSE file at the repository root for the full license text, adding no narrower condition or restriction.
- Packaging metadata consistency (vqultolm, vutylkzu): the README is packaging metadata force-included in the vsix alongside the manifest and outside .vscodeignore's control, not a runtime payload file loaded by the extension; neither README.md nor nsyxzxzr may present the README as a runtime file or deny that it ships.

3. READABLE, USER-FOCUSED PROSE (NO IMPLEMENTATION OR SCHEMA JARGON).
README.md is user-facing documentation, and oxxwkrvo commits the features section to user-facing terms. Both README.md and nsyxzxzr's description of what the README presents must be written in readable, user-focused prose rather than reciting internal node-JSON schema property names, schema token rosters, layout tie-break formulas, webview HTML hosting mechanics or raw JSON edge-inversion mechanics. Fail with a finding naming the offending element and oxxwkrvo if README.md (or nsyxzxzr's commitment for what README.md states) includes any of the following:
- dotted node-JSON property names or raw schema-field literals such as 'content.type', 'content.ref' or '"inline"' (for example 'as content.type spells it' or 'when content.ref is a list of repo-relative paths rather than "inline"');
- internal content.type token lists ('text, ears and review-criteria', 'visual-spec, json-schema, test and rust') enumerated to define prose versus monospaced rendering;
- the internal layout sort tie-breaking formula ('by topological depth from the roots, then initial left-to-right position, then node id');
- HTML webview implementation mechanics (such as describing the graph as 'drawn as an HTML page');
- raw JSON field-lookup and edge-inversion mechanics (such as 'the ids its depends_on names', 'the ids its evaluates names', 'whose depends_on names the selected node', 'whose evaluates names it', or 'read the same depends_on and evaluates edges from the other end, with the parent-to-child direction fixing which end each list holds').
Naming the user-visible UI labels themselves ('Deccy: Open Deccy Graph', 'Kind', 'Content', 'Rationale', 'depends_on', 'evaluates', 'dependents', 'evaluators'), the search keys ('/', 'Enter', 'Shift+Enter', 'Esc'), 'Apache-2.0' and 'LICENSE' is user-facing and permitted.

HOW THE CHECK IS APPLIED.
Read README.md and nodes/nsyxzxzr.json against uuutyrzs, rzkvnnll, oxxwkrvo, ynmpvmmp, rolozxtn, vqultolm and vutylkzu; nothing runs. Quoting, paraphrasing, reordering and grouping sentences or bullets are free so long as all required sections and user-facing facts are present, the prose is user-focused without the forbidden implementation or schema jargon, and no claim contradicts or overreaches the seven prerequisites.
content.rationale: The dependent nsyxzxzr refs README.md, repository-root documentation that commits in readable prose, so it is natural-layer. uuutyrzs, rzkvnnll, oxxwkrvo, ynmpvmmp, rolozxtn and vqultolm are inline natural-layer prose decisions, so their edges sit in the eval-matrix's natural-to-natural gate cell; vutylkzu refs .vscodeignore (a code-layer artifact) used by a natural-layer child, an unknown cell in the eval-matrix that takes the default cell: the gate form, flagged for a matrix entry. One evaluation covers the seven-prerequisite fan-out because nsyxzxzr's use of all seven is a single composition: a title and introduction grounded in uuutyrzs, four named sections grounded in rzkvnnll, oxxwkrvo, ynmpvmmp and rolozxtn, and the README's role as packaged repository metadata grounded in vqultolm and vutylkzu. This amendment is required because oxxwkrvo has been refined to commit the README's features section to user-facing terms rather than internal schema and implementation mechanics, and nsyxzxzr is being refined to compose README.md in readable, user-focused prose. The previous criterion in tmmsqyqm evaluated nsyxzxzr against oxxwkrvo's old commitment and explicitly demanded that README.md recite dotted node-JSON property names and literals (content.type, content.ref, "inline"), internal schema type-token rosters (text, ears, review-criteria, visual-spec, json-schema, test, rust), the internal layout sort tie-break formula (topological depth from the roots, then initial left-to-right position, then node id), and raw JSON edge-lookup phrasing. Under that old gate, a user-focused README.md that follows the refined oxxwkrvo would fail, while the current jargon-heavy README.md would pass. The amended criterion aligns the features subject floor with the refined oxxwkrvo, preserves the completeness floor, composition bound and closed licences across all seven prerequisites, and requires readable, user-focused prose free of internal schema property names, type-token lists, layout tie-break formulas, HTML webview mechanics and raw JSON edge-inversion phrasing. The check is applied by reading README.md and nodes/nsyxzxzr.json against the seven prerequisites; nothing runs. This second amendment is the rename: uuutyrzs has been refined to record the extension as deccy-viewer, displayed as "Deccy Viewer", and nsyxzxzr is refined so that README.md's title and introduction name it so. The previous criterion quoted uuutyrzs's pre-rename subject verbatim inside its introduction rule — that vsc-deccy is a VS Code extension that visualises the deccy graph of a project and the connections between nodes beyond what a jj graph shows — so it judged the title and introduction against the old identity rather than the recorded one: a README whose title and introduction still carried the pre-rename name satisfied the quoted subject, while a README naming deccy-viewer / "Deccy Viewer" read as naming something the quoted subject did not license, so the old gate would have passed a stale README and failed a correct one. The amended rule names no identity of its own and quotes no name: it requires the title and introduction to carry the identity uuutyrzs records and no other, with the title displaying the recorded display name and the introduction identifying the extension by the recorded package name or display name, so a title or introduction carrying an identity or name uuutyrzs does not record is a finding whatever that name is, and a later rename needs no gate edit. Because the refined uuutyrzs carries the connections-between-nodes fact in its rationale rather than in its subject, that statement is permitted and its absence is not a finding, rather than being required as before. No other rule in the criterion named or presupposed the pre-rename identity: the packaging-metadata rule (vqultolm, vutylkzu) and the readable-prose rule (oxxwkrvo) speak of the extension and of user-visible labels without naming it, and the completeness floor, composition bound, the rzkvnnll, oxxwkrvo, ynmpvmmp, rolozxtn, vqultolm and vutylkzu subject floors and licences, and the readable-prose rules are otherwise unchanged in substance.
